title: SLIDE links islet T-cell clone expansion to immune gene programs
summary: SLIDE, an interpretable latent-factor interaction method, was applied to paired single-cell RNA-seq and T-cell receptor data from islet-derived CD4 T cells in NOD mice. The analysis identified latent components associated with clonal expansion and grouped inhibitory-receptor and intracellular signaling/apoptosis-related genes among the associated programs. The result is an inference from existing multiomic data, not a causal perturbation; it is a distinct T1D application in the same article as the separately catalogued systemic-sclerosis analysis.
ai_technology: SLIDE interpretable latent-factor interaction discovery and exploration

evidence.tested: The method was applied to paired single-cell RNA-seq/TCR-seq from islet-derived CD4 T cells in NOD mice; the analysis reports latent components associated with clone expansion and compares the findings against an independent published dataset and alternative methods.
evidence.unknown: The inferred gene programs are associations from existing data; the T1D analysis does not prospectively perturb the proposed pathways or establish causality.
evidence.ai_role: SLIDE uses interpretable machine learning to identify interactions among latent factors in high-dimensional omics data and was applied to connect T-cell gene programs with clonal expansion.

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Methods indexed full article, including T1D application, Methods, results, author affiliations and publication/version dates; PubMed primary abstract and affiliation metadata.

relationships.reason: Both records cite the same SLIDE article. This record describes its distinct T1D islet T-cell analysis; the linked record describes the systemic-sclerosis keratinocyte analysis. The relationship identifies a shared paper without asserting the results are identical or independent papers.
